issues.html:
🔗Matrix Live S13E17 Bring your Matrix chats to emClient

We recently learned about emClient adding Matrix support, so this week Andy talked to Michal Burger about why they joined the Matrix ecosystem.

🔗Dept of Status of Matrix 🌡️

🔗Matrix.org Privacy Policy update

Andy P reports

There have been a few updates to The Matrix.org Foundation Privacy Policy (note that this document also applies to the matrix.org homeserver).

3.4.0 - update 2.1, 2.2 and 2.6 following MAS migration (legal basis, account and authentication data, IP logging); add 2.2.3 on Synapse usage statistics; update 2.11 on AWS, Amazon SES and Cloudflare, including Trust & Safety content scanning; update registered address; update third-party links; numbering, spelling and consistency fixes - November 2026

If you have an account on the matrix.org homeserver, or want to understand the Foundation's policies, please have a look. We'll continue to refine our legal documents to make them more clear and accessible.

🔗Dept of Events and Talks 🗣️

🔗Digital Resilience Europe (website)

Andy P says

The Digital Resilience Europe Conference is happening on Dec 2-3 2026 in Paris, France. The Matrix.org Foundation will be represented on-stage by Amandine with her session "Sustainable Digital Sovereignty: learnings from Matrix".

We also have a table in the SuperStack Village at the event, so drop by if you are attending!

🔗Stammtische (website)

HarHarLinks reports

A Stammtisch ("regular's table") is a German meetup format where those with a shared interest meet regularly for discussion, exchange, and socialising.

Find more community organised events at matrix-community.events!

  • 30 November (but usually 3rd Monday of every month) 19:00 CET: #matrix-stammtisch:ccc-ffm.de at CCC FFM.
  • 1 December (Tuesday every 4 weeks), 19:00 CET: #matrix-dortmund:matrix.org at Chaostreff Dortmund. learn more

Are you running a Matrix meetup? Add it to the list!

🔗Dept of Spec 📜

Andrew Morgan (anoa) {he/him} says

Here's your weekly spec update! The heart of Matrix is the specification - and this is modified by Matrix Spec Change (MSC) proposals. Learn more about how the process works at https://spec.matrix.org/proposals.

🔗MSC Status

New MSCs:

  • MSC4588: Exactly 256 bits for m.secret_storage.v1.aes-hmac-sha2
  • MSC4587: Relaxing requirements for reauthentication on cross-signing-key upload
  • MSC4586: Flag to explicitly persist URL preview assets

MSCs in Final Comment Period:

  • No MSCs are in FCP.

Accepted MSCs:

  • MSC4576: Only allow data publishing when also allowing audio/video publishing on LiveKit transports
  • MSC4437: Endpoint to replace entire profile

Closed MSCs:

  • No MSCs were closed/rejected this week.

🔗Spec Updates

Happy (late) Thanksgiving! 🦃

On the menu for this week are two new cryptography-related MSCs, and one about fixing an edge case when loading URL preview images. Check them out over the weekend!

Otherwise we had another Matrix 2.0 MSC merge (MSC4576)! As well as an improvement for clients to update profiles quickly (MSC4437).

A familiar call out to for anyone who likes writing spec. We need spec PRs written for all the accepted Matrix 2.0 MSCs! The full list of those without spec PRs can be found here. Thank you!

🔗Dept of Servers 🏢

🔗Zendrite (website)

pat-s announces

Zendrite, the Dendrite fork written in Go, released v3.10.0. This release adds room retention policies, more MatrixRTC support and new moderation tools.

Retention and moderation

  • MSC1763 room retention policies: events past a room's retention policy are no longer served in sync, over federation or in /notifications, and are purged from the database.
  • MSC4194 lets moderators redact a user's events in a room, and MSC4293 redacts them as part of a kick or ban.
  • Refused sends and membership changes now name the reason (MSC3848).

MatrixRTC

  • Zendrite now issues LiveKit tokens itself, removes departed members from LiveKit SFUs and delegates delayed leaves (MSC4195, MatrixRTC with a LiveKit backend).
  • The stable rtc/transports endpoint from MSC4143, which tells clients which RTC transports the server offers.
  • Push rules ring for MatrixRTC call notifications (MSC4075).

Application services and clients

  • Application services receive to-device events (MSC4203), answer key queries for their users (MSC3983, MSC3984) and can serve parts of the APIs (MSC4512).
  • Clients can replace a whole profile (MSC4437), query several profiles at once (MSC4536) and delete account data (MSC3391).
  • Push rules can match on related events (MSC3664).
  • Operators can opt in to refusing access tokens in query strings (MSC4127) and to limiting key queries to users who share a room (MSC4263).

Federation and fixes

  • Ambiguous federation JSON is rejected (MSC4458), well-known redirects are followed only over https (MSC4402) and EDUs are limited to 64 KiB (MSC4514).
  • Room version 12 invites whose stripped state lacks m.room.create are rejected.
  • Sliding sync keeps to-device messages past its limit and sends typing and receipts only for joined rooms.
  • /register now requires the UIA session the server issued.
  • Guests can accept federated invites.
  • The docs moved to docs.zendrite.xyz.

Release notes: https://codefloe.com/pat-s/zendrite/releases/tag/v3.10.0
Chat: #matrix:zendrite.xyz

🔗Dept of Clients 📱

🔗Element X iOS (website)

A total rewrite of Element iOS using the Matrix Rust SDK underneath and targeting devices running iOS 17+.

Mauro announces

Hi everyone! Here's what the Element X iOS team has been up to this week:

🔗✨ New and improved

  • Custom emoji: you can now react with a room's own emoji from the reaction picker and search them by shortcode. Room details also has a new "Emoji and stickers" screen where you can browse the room's packs.
  • Reaction celebrations: the particle effects we were trying out are now on for everyone, with gentler floating hearts. They stay off when Reduce Motion is on.
  • iPhone Duo: the app now uses the standard tab bar, which fits the Duo much better.

🔗🚧 In progress

  • Multi-account support: the verification and sign-out screens now show which account they're for, and a verification request can appear whichever account you're using. If an account is signed out from another device, a screen now tells you which one.
  • Stickers: sending stickers from a room's sticker packs is coming next.
  • Sharing: we're redesigning the share sheet so you can pick up to five chats and send to all of them at once.

🔗🐛 Fixes

  • Files shared into the app from apps like Files now keep their original name.
  • Fixed a crash when sharing to the app while a picture was open full screen.
  • The keyboard no longer stays on top of a call when you go from picture-in-picture to full screen.
  • Custom emoji and image reactions now follow the "hide media in the timeline" setting.

🔗💜 Community

  • Thanks to @wykeenjenga for letting you swipe away the media preview while it's still loading.

🔗Sennit (website)

Eric announces

I'm building Sennit, a Matrix client for people who use a lot of bridges. Point it at your homeserver and your mautrix bridges, and the same person on WhatsApp, Signal and Telegram becomes one conversation, with a small badge on each message showing which network it came through. Bridge logins, QR codes included, run inside the app through the bridgev2 provisioning API, so there's no bot chat to drive.

This week:

  • OAuth / next-gen sign-in. Servers that only offer OIDC, like Continuwuity behind an identity provider, now open their own login page and hand you back to Sennit. Thanks to the person on r/matrixdotorg who reported it.
  • Sync between devices. Merged chats and settings follow you to your other devices, encrypted with your key backup, so the homeserver only stores ciphertext.
  • Sennit Web. Your phone serves the app to a paired browser on your network, end-to-end encrypted, with nothing hosted.
  • Hindi and Arabic (right to left) joined the other six languages.

It runs on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Linux and is AGPL-3.0-only. Store builds have an optional one-time purchase for the AI features; a build from source has everything. It's still beta and rough in places, so feedback is very welcome in #sennit:matrix.aachen.dev.

GitHub

🔗Dept of VoIP 🤙

🔗Element Call (website)

Native Decentralised End-to-end Encrypted Group Calls in Matrix.

Timo K. says

This week we shipped v0.29.0 of Element Call. As already mentioned last week, background effects are now here! The camera menu now has a grid of effects. You can blur your background, pick one of the built-in backgrounds, or upload your own images (they stay on your device). There's also a live camera preview in the menu.

This release also contains a lot of changes how our device management works. This results in fixes for device switching in Chrome and a smoother transition from lobby to in-call.

Also new: support for the spec compliant m.livekit MatrixRTC transport prefix, and an experimental React component on npm (@element-hq/element-call-component) that will allow a more native integration of Element Call into Element Web.

With this release we also welcome our first-time contributors RaphaelFakhri and junkerderprovinz!

Release notes: https://github.com/element-hq/element-call/releases/tag/v0.29.0

🔗Dept of SDKs and Frameworks 🧰

🔗libQuotient (website)

A Qt6 library to write cross-platform clients for Matrix.

kitsune reports

🔗libQuotient 0.10 beta

The day has finally come - the first libQuotient beta riding on matrix-rust-sdk-crypto instead of libolm! Massive kudos to @tobiasfella:kde.org for doing most of the E2EE heavylifting and for making Rust/C++ interface actually work across platforms. Also on the list: better QML integration and some more incremental features as well as improvements in stability and performance. The release notes have it all: https://github.com/quotient-im/libQuotient/releases/tag/0.10-beta1

🔗Dept of Ops 🛠

🔗botanica (website)

alexia starling says

botanica 0.0.3-alpha is out!

botanica is a small, fedora-based OS aimed at giving you all the software you need in one package to run a chatserver at home, based on continuwuity, sable, and meowlnir for moderation

lots of things were added or changed in this release! you can see the full changelog on forge.starlightnet.work

most notably, meowlnir is now included, unbound is configured by default as the default resolver, and the built-in docs were slightly altered to give more info to the user :)

and also, there is now a real, in-production botanica instance at https://matrix.cyrneko.eu ! I have put my own self-hosted setup onto botanica to test, and thus far the instance has been running remarkably well :)

🔗Dept of Community Posts ✍🏻

🔗Improvements to the MSC progress charts

MTRNord (they/them) announces

There is some update on the spec graph page I made a while back for TWIM based on Anoa's and Matthew's prior work.

Due to nerdsniping by Kim I added support for the same graph Matthew showed in the last State of the Union talk as well as adding some word clouds based on the comments.

You can find them over at https://matrix-spec.stats.mtrnord.blog/ if you are into more graph goodness for Spec :)

issues.title: This Week in Matrix 2026-11-20
issues.html:
🔗Matrix Live - MatrixMedia for Content Creators

Andy interviews Lillia and Artem from MatrixMedia. Lillia attended The Matrix Conference to get to know the community, and this episode of Matrix Live explores their work building tools for content creators that sit alongside regular Matrix services.

🔗Dept of Status of Matrix 🌡️

🔗New Foundation Members

Amandine reports

This week we are announcing two new members of the Foundation! 🚀

Nordeck IT + Consulting (or Nordeck for short) is one of the first companies to have made the choice to add Matrix to their expertise (back in 2018 I think), and today probably one of the biggest pools of Matrix experts available for consulting in the ecosystem. They’re also a huge contributor of volunteers across the board, but in particular as part of the Working Groups 🫶. Beyond consulting for various projects, they also build NeoBoard and keep growing their NeoToolSuite with more and more widgets 🤖. We’re delighted that Hato & the team are officially joining the Foundation as Silver members!

FLOSS/fund is dedicated to supporting critical, impactful, and valuable Free/Libre and Open Source projects globally and we’re very happy they have decided to support Matrix, amongst many other projects, and join us as Silver members! 💚

🎉 Welcome both and thank you for your support!

🔗Dept of Events and Talks 🗣️

🔗FOSDEM 2027 (website)

Andy P says

Preparations for FOSDEM 2027 are underway! At the time that this edition of This Week In Matrix is going live on the blog, there are still a few hours remaining in the Call for Proposals for the Decentralised Messaging Devroom - the call closes at 23:55 UTC 20th November 2026.

In addition, we are happy to confirm that The Matrix.org Foundation will again have a stand at FOSDEM on both days (Saturday 30th and Sunday 31st January). We are always grateful to the community volunteers who help to staff our presence at FOSDEM, and if you are able to offer your time on the stand, our volunteering tool will open for signups in the near future.

One more thing! We'll have a whole day of additional Matrix content on the FOSDEM fringe on Friday 29th January. More information on this (format and location) will be coming soon, but if you're already planning your trip to Brussels, it will be worth knowing about.

🔗Dept of Spec 📜

Andrew Morgan (anoa) {he/him} reports

Here's your weekly spec update! The heart of Matrix is the specification - and this is modified by Matrix Spec Change (MSC) proposals. Learn more about how the process works at https://spec.matrix.org/proposals.

🔗MSC Status

New MSCs:

  • MSC4584: Soft-ignoring
  • MSC4583: Minimum power level to send state
  • MSC4582: Require the m.room_versions capability

MSCs in Final Comment Period:

  • MSC4576: Only allow data publishing when also allowing audio/video publishing on LiveKit transports (merge)
  • MSC4437: Endpoint to replace entire profile (merge)

Accepted MSCs:

  • MSC4492: Clarify that pagination tokens are directionless
  • MSC4388: Secure out-of-band channel for sign in with QR

Closed MSCs:

  • No MSCs were closed/rejected this week.

🔗Spec Updates

A fair few MSCs moving through the pipeline this week! Most notably, I'm excited to see MSC4388: Secure out-of-band channel for sign in with QR, part of the login-with-QR-code work, finally being accepted! That MSC was the final dependent of MSC4108, the main QR login MSC. Looking forward to seeing that one land soon!

Despite this excitement, the SCT is still mostly keeping their attention on Matrix 2.0 MSCs. One of those, MSC4576: Only allow data publishing when also allowing audio/video publishing on LiveKit transports, has landed in FCP merge this week!

The remaining two are MSC4480: Sliding Sync Extension: Sticky Events (some comment threads need pushing forward from reviewers) and MSC4075: MatrixRTC invites and notifications (likewise).

And another reminder that we need spec PRs written for all the accepted MSCs! The full list of Matrix 2.0 MSCs without spec PRs can be found here. Thanks!

🔗Dept of Servers 🏢

🔗Zendrite (website)

Zendrite is a Matrix homeserver written in Go.

pat-s reports

Zendrite now has its own Matrix space: #matrix:zendrite.xyz

  • #announcements:zendrite.xyz for releases and project news
  • #help:zendrite.xyz for questions about installing and running Zendrite
  • #development:zendrite.xyz for development chat

v3.9 is out, with a focus on federation and notifications:

  • Faster remote room joins on the joining side (MSC3902), and partial-state send_join responses for other servers (MSC3706)
  • Invite filtering (MSC4155) and invite reasons in createRoom (MSC4491)
  • Profile updates in /sync (MSC4429)
  • Remote toggling of push notifications (MSC3881), and push rules for polls and encrypted events (MSC3930, MSC4028)
  • Moderator access to redacted event content (MSC2815)

Coming in the next release:

  • Sliding sync on /v4/sync, with the accepted extensions and the MSC4551 receipt rules
  • Batch profile lookups (MSC4536) and whole-profile replacement (MSC4437)
  • Redacting all of a user's events in a room (MSC4194)
  • Ringing for MatrixRTC call notifications (MSC4075) and the stable rtc/transports endpoint (MSC4143)
  • To-device events and key queries for application services (MSC4203, MSC3983, MSC3984)

The full list of supported MSCs is on the MSC support page. Releases and container images are on Codefloe.

🔗Dept of Bridges 🌉

🔗Bolt / Lightning

jersey says

Bolt and Lightning v0.9.8 are out!

This release features support for reactions, pins, DM replies for sensitive commands on Matrix (matching how the bot works on other platforms), and a bunch of other features for other platforms as well. Additionally, my singular brain cell was hard at work fixing some bugs affecting Matrix support, bringing you better emoji fallbacks and spec-compliant escaped localparts when it's in appservice mode.

Lightning is an open-source bridge bot and bot framework which supports Discord, Spacebar, Harmony, Fluxer, Stoat, Telegram, Matrix, IRC (including IRCv3 magic), Osmium, Matterbridge's API, and its own REST API, in addition to Matrix. Bolt is the free hosted version I offer that supports the platforms above, with Libera.chat and OFTC being the two currently supported IRC networks.

You can find more in the changelog, lightning website, bolt website, codeberg repo, or in https://matrix.to/#/#bolt:ineedmore.money and https://matrix.to/#/#lightning:ineedmore.money

🔗Dept of Clients 📱

🔗WizardChat (website)

j20a05n reports

Hi TWIM! We'd like to introduce WizardChat, an open-source, end-to-end encrypted Matrix client built for communities that want to leave Discord without giving up voice rooms, screen sharing or soundboards. It runs on the web, on Windows, macOS and Linux, and as native apps on iOS and Android.

Every app shares one Rust core built on matrix-rust-sdk. It's compiled to WASM for the web, wrapped with Tauri on desktop, and bound through UniFFI to SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose on mobile. Calls use MatrixRTC with LiveKit, with push to talk everywhere (system-wide on desktop), screen sharing with system audio, and an experimental on-device noise filter based on RNNoise. In calls there's also a soundboard (MSC4577) with custom sound packs, and Watch Together for YouTube with a shared queue, both synced over the call's data channel. Beyond calls, there are custom emoji and sticker packs, pronouns and a different name in each room or space, a theme editor, and QR and OAuth login.

Try it in your browser or grab an app from the downloads. Android is on F-Droid and Obtainium, with a Google Play beta running, and iOS can be sideloaded while the App Store review is pending. You can find the source code on GitLab.

🔗Element X iOS (website)

A total rewrite of Element iOS using the Matrix Rust SDK underneath and targeting devices running iOS 17+.

Doug says

Exciting news for iOS users this week as our multi-account support is starting to take shape! Much of the underlying code has been made account-aware, and the Settings screen has received the new component for switching accounts, so we’ve wired up the add account flow under a feature flag for the first time. It’s still very much a work in progress as there are many flows to review and update before it’s fully ready, but it’s great to see it working after lots of refactoring. Other notable changes to report include:

  • Call screens are now presented independently of the user session screens, meaning you’ll be able to join a call for account A and use a PiP whilst checking messages in account B.
  • Recovery and verification flows have had a general tidy-up to make them more helpful and consistent with the other Element clients.
  • We’ve been experimenting with particle effects on reactions and now support the rendering of data-mx-emoticon images in both reactions and message bubbles.
  • In the timeline, date separators are now exposed as headings to VoiceOver, making it quick to navigate between days. The loading indicator also no longer flickers in between pagination requests.
  • We’ve updated CI to use Xcode 27.2, meaning we can now start to tweak the layout on iPhone Duo. We’ve been building for the Duo since launch but needed the CI changes to actually use the new APIs.

🔗Element X Android (website)

Android Matrix messenger application using the Matrix Rust SDK and Jetpack Compose.

Jorge reports

Hello everyone, this week the Element X Android team has been working on:

  • Allowing users to set a custom font size for messages in the timeline, so if you have issues reading your messages you can just make the text of the timeline larger without changing the whole system font size.
  • Improving how the 'you were signed out' screen works with multi-account and displaying which account will be logged out on the 'remove this device' flow.
  • We reworked the recovery setup flow a bit so the UX is better.
  • The new timeline renderer will also be used to display plain text messages when it's enabled, handling link detection and adding mention and room pills using the new logic. Also, it will be enabled by default soon for those testing the nightlies!
  • A PR for adding timeline animations was added. Special thanks to bxdxnn, the contributor who created the original implementation that got us working on this. These will also be enabled by default in nightlies soon.

And of course, we worked on ironing out some bugs you reported. Thanks!

🔗Tammy (website)

Multiplatform messenger built on top of Trixnity Messenger.

Benedict reports

It has been a while, and it was worth the wait, a brand-new Tammy release is finally here!

🔗MatrixRTC Calls

As teased in Matthew's The Matrix State of the Union, Tammy now brings basic MatrixRTC (LiveKit) call support on Android and Web! You can now start and join calls right from Tammy, and a handy indicator in the room list lets you spot rooms with active calls at a glance.

🔗Spaces

Tammy now includes basic support for Spaces, helping you bring some much-needed order to your chats. Right now, this lets you browse and view your Spaces with plenty more Space features already on the horizon!

🔗Stickers & Inline Images

You can now view, add, remove, and favorite stickers right inside Tammy, while custom emotes and inline images render cleanly in both messages and formatted reply previews.

🔗Better UX for Reactions

Tammy now renders custom image reactions cleanly (no raw mxc:// URLs anymore)! Reaction piles also align neatly with your message bubbles and visually reflect their current state (such as sending, by-me, etc.). Best of all, taking back a reaction offline or while it's still in the outbox now works reliably, leaving no temporary ghost emojis behind.

🔗SQLite in Web

Web performance just got a solid upgrade: new accounts on the Web client now use SQLite-backed Room database storage, running in its own dedicated worker for a noticeably snappier experience!

🔗Bugfixes & Internal Improvements

As always, we also fixed a bunch of bugs and made plenty of improvements under the hood to keep everything running smoothly.

🔗Dept of VoIP 🤙

🔗Element Call (website)

Native Decentralised End-to-end Encrypted Group Calls in Matrix.

Timo K. reports

The VoIP team has been very busy, but few of the things we worked on were easy to present. Now we finally have something available on call.element.dev that motivated us to write a TWIM entry:

The new UX for adding video backgrounds has landed.

We are very happy with how it turned out. Feel free to play around with it: https://call-next.element.io/ !

Besides this, we are making a lot of progress on refactoring our codebase. We have big plans for a unified RTC Rust SDK (check out the related Matrix Conference talk if you are interested) now that the spec is stable. There will be a lot more coming in the future, we are seeing the light at the end of the R&D tunnel (and iterating on the MatrixRTC spec). Now that we are free from the foundational work of equipping Matrix with a super flexible real-time solution, the VoIP team at Element is excited to work on new features.

🔗Dept of SDKs and Frameworks 🧰

🔗Trixnity (website)

Multiplatform Kotlin SDK for developing Clients, Bots, Appservices and Servers.

Benedict says

Trixnity has had a massive run of releases over the last few months, packing in Matrix 1.19 support, a major MatrixRTC push, and plenty of hardening under the hood!

🔗MatrixRTC & Calling Foundations

Trixnity now ships the core building blocks for MatrixRTC! Across these releases, we added support for MSC4140 (cancellable delayed events), MSC4195 (LiveKit transport), MSC4196 (voice and video calling application events), and MSC4143 (MatrixRTC). Additionally, several updates for MSC4354 (sticky events) have been implemented.

🔗Room3 & Web Persistence

Trixnity upgraded to Room3 and now supports Room repositories on the Web! We also boosted database reliability and speed by deduplicating state event saves, chunking receipts and oversized transactions, and waiting cleanly for client completion before closing the database.

🔗And More

Alongside minor features such as stickers, there are, of course, plenty of bug fixes and internal improvements.

🔗Dept of Ops 🛠

🔗botanica (website)

soweli leia reports

announcing 0.0.2-alpha of botanica!

botanica is a small, fedora-based OS that I’ve been slowly chipping away on, which’s end-goal is to make it easier to self-host matrix at home by taking out the work of finding the right software, setting it up yourself, and maintaining the system.

it builds on fedora-bootc, so you get atomic updates, rollbacks, and the ability to switch to another image at any time, or extend it!

it’s still very, very work-in-progress, many things are still unimplemented or don’t work quite right, but the basics to configure continuwuity and sable are there, and with a bit of manual work getting it connected to the wider internet, it can federate!

it comes with a small TUI written in python+textual, called flower. it’s aim is to make first-time-setup easier while also providing basic system utilities, like doing updates or checking on the status of various system services.

and finally, it’s in desperate need of more than one person working on it 😵‍💫; but I’m hopeful that’ll change over time!

you can find more about it at https://botanica.starlightnet.work, and source code at https://forge.starlightnet.work/Team/botanica; The project is AI:0

🔗Dept of Community Posts ✍🏻

🔗Matrix flyers

MTRNord (they/them) says

I have something... unusual to publish for once!

https://mtrnord.blog/2026/11/19/i-made-a-matrix-flyer/

I decided to build and print Matrix specific flyers I can hand out at events :) I also wrote a blog post a bit about the history of me trying to do that and showcasing my thought process on this and why I decided to make one.

I hope people enjoy it as much as I do. I plan to bring them to the next FOSDEM if all things go to plan :)

issues.html:
🔗Matrix Live S13E15 - Website & Content Working Group updates

This episode, we're talking about the work of the Website & Content Working Group, and having a look behind the scenes in the production of This Week in Matrix itself. You can also read the news entry that is added during this video, down below!

Woah - a Matrix Live about This Week in Matrix, in This Week in Matrix... it feels like some kind of Inception scenario... 😎

🔗Dept of Status of Matrix 🌡️

🔗Governing Board (website)

The Governing Board is an advisory board to The Matrix.org Foundation and with elected representatives from all across the Matrix ecosystem.

HarHarLinks announces

Happy Friday, TWIM! It's been roundabout half a year since the last meeting and report from the Governing Board, though you might have been following this cycle's election process in May and June. I'm honored to follow in Greg's footsteps and announce the news this time as the Board's new chair, with a lot of support from our new vice-chair richvdh, and I am very grateful to Rich for taking the time to write up the report for you. 🙏 The Board gathered last week for its second meeting of the year for a comprehensive exchange of highlights in the Matrix world. As usual, you can find the comprehensive account in the blog post. We'd love to receive your feedback and questions - you can always find us at #governing-board-office:matrix.org.

If you'd like to learn more about how to get involved in the Foundation, the Governing Board, its members, structure, activities, Committees, Working Groups, or anything else, you can read a lot about this in the Foundation section right here on the matrix.org website. We're always excited about new ideas and initiatives - it's all of the ecosystem collaborating that really pushes Matrix forward.

Finally, in case you missed it until now, also watch the Foundation & Governing Board update from The Matrix Conference!

🔗Dept of Events and Talks 🗣️

🔗Stammtische (website)

HarHarLinks says

A Stammtisch ("regular's table") is a German meetup format where those with a shared interest meet regularly for discussion, exchange, and socialising.

Find more community organised events at matrix-community.events!

  • 19 November (3rd Thursday of every month) 19:00 CET: #matrix-stammtisch:freiburg.social at Blauer Fuchs. Learn more.
  • 19 November, 19:00 CET: #matrix-stammtisch:dresden.network at ro7. Learn more

Are you running a Matrix meetup? Add it to the list!

🔗FOSDEM 2027 (website)

Andy P says

FOSDEM will take place January 30-31, 2027 in Brussels.

A reminder that you have one more week to submit a proposal to the Decentralised Messaging Devroom! Check our blog post for the details. The deadline for submissions is 20 November.

More to come on FOSDEM very soon!

🔗Dept of Working Groups 💪

🔗Website & Content Working Group (website)

The Website and Content Working Group is responsible for the editorial and technical oversight of the main Matrix websites and social media channels.

MTRNord (they/them) reports

It has been 4 months since our last update and not only did we spend this time on lots of changes on the conference website but also we improved lots of other areas on the websites for you to enjoy!

🔗Overhauled Ecosystem Design

In the last update we already had major updates to the try-matrix page and also some improvements landed on the ecosystem pages. Since then we took this a step further and adapted the try-matrix design language also in the ecosystem. This means specifically for you:

  • A new Featured clients section matching try-matrix
  • Color coded pills 🌈
  • Better support for SPDX license definitions
  • Improved filtering (more colour!)
  • A better overview of available features in clients - if you spot a ❔ icon and know about that client supporting that feature, click the link on the bottom of the page to let us know!
  • Screenshots are back!
  • Big improvements to the bridges
    • Obsolete bridges are visually hidden
    • Clearer feature support
  • Better unified design across all ecosystem pages
  • Breadcrumbs to more easily navigate subpages

🔗Other Changes to matrix.org

Apart from the big ecosystem update there have also be plenty of other changes.

Many thanks to all contributors helping us keep the ecosystem data up to date, including @clins1994, @Mizerd, @dfuchss, @SpiritCroc, @bones-was-here, @wigmarbled, and @subpop! Thanks to you, our ecosystem directory keeps growing and existing entries stay accurate. ❤️

We've also been doing regular maintenance to keep the Foundation, Governing Board, and Working Group information fresh, including adding two new Working Groups and updating information about existing ones.

On the technical side, we've done some housekeeping, including cleaning up our metadata templates, ensuring our matrix.to links follow the specification, and updating our content contribution guidelines with more information on how we handle media on the website.

We also introduced a new policy for ecosystem listings: projects now need to have been active and supported Matrix for at least three months before being considered for inclusion. This should help us ensure that projects listed in the ecosystem are actively maintained and have demonstrated support for Matrix.

🔗A New Native Schedule System for the Conference Website

Another big change we did land in this timeframe has been the native schedule for The Matrix Conference website. This feature not only allowed us better visual integration into the conference page but also allows us to have new features which weren't possible before.

As a result we now have a new schedule which should be more accessible and bring more data sources together, we have the schedule also visible on the new live streaming page design (you'd have to catch it during the conference!) and last but not least we now have proper schedule widgets usable alongside the streams in rooms to support the remote conference experience.

🔗Other Changes to the Conference Website

Like with the matrix.org page here have been also a lot of smaller changes. Most prominently the team did an amazing job at ensuring the recordings were listed quickly as the conference ended, we overhauled both the livestream and the recordings page and we also improved our tooling around the recordings ingest to the page to reduce our turnaround times in the future.

🔗What Else Happened in the Working group?

Beyond the actual work on the websites, we also want to welcome xeni to the Working Group as our newest member who has joined us after helping us at The Matrix Conference 2026!

🔗If You Want to Contribute

If you want to contribute yourself to this feel free to check out both the website repository and the conference website repository or join us in our room at #matrix.org-website:matrix.org.

🔗Dept of Spec 📜

Andrew Morgan (anoa) {he/him} reports

Here's your weekly spec update! The heart of Matrix is the specification - and this is modified by Matrix Spec Change (MSC) proposals. Learn more about how the process works at https://spec.matrix.org/proposals.

🔗MSC Status

New MSCs:

  • MSC4581: Media annotations and universal alt text

MSCs in Final Comment Period:

  • MSC4492: Clarify that pagination tokens are directionless (merge)
  • MSC4388: Secure out-of-band channel for sign in with QR (merge)

Accepted MSCs:

  • No MSCs were accepted this week.

Closed MSCs:

  • No MSCs were closed/rejected this week.

🔗Spec Updates

The Spec Core Team have been laser-focused on Matrix 2.0 work post-conference. We're hoping to get the 2.0 release out in the next few weeks.

Of the... 37(!) total MSCs marked matrix-2.0 on the matrix-spec-proposals repo, there are 3 MSCs that have yet to be accepted and 9 MSCs which need a spec PR written.

Help is welcome, especially on the spec PR writing! A spec PR is the transformation from an MSC's free-form proposal text to the terse language of the Matrix spec (found in this repo).

On the MSC-acceptance side, MSC4576: Only allow data publishing when also allowing audio/video publishing on LiveKit transports is relatively uncontroversial, and likely just needs more eyes from the SCT.

The other two needs some more discussion, but they're close! Watch this space for the thrilling conclusion soon!

🔗Dept of Servers 🏢

🔗Zendrite (website)

pat-s reports

Zendrite, the Dendrite fork written in Go, released v3.9.0. This release brings faster remote room joins and a long list of newly supported MSCs.

Faster remote joins

  • MSC3902: Zendrite now implements the joining side of faster remote room joins, where a server joins with partial room state.
  • MSC3706: Zendrite also serves partial-state send_join responses to other servers.
  • Joins to rooms with a malformed allow list are refused instead of answering 500.
  • send_join and send_leave events are no longer echoed back to their sender.

Spec support

  • MSC4155 invite filtering.
  • MSC3881 remote toggling of push notifications, and MSC3890 removal of local notification settings when a device is deleted.
  • MSC4429 profile updates in /sync.
  • MSC2815, which gives moderators access to the content of redacted events.
  • MSC3874 relation type and MSC2326 label event filters.
  • MSC3930 poll and MSC4028 encrypted event push rules.
  • MSC4446 moving the fully read marker backwards, MSC4502 targeted room member queries and MSC4491 invite reasons in createRoom.
  • The room version org.matrix.msc3389.10 from MSC3389 is offered, and the unimplemented MSC4242 room version is no longer supported.

Sliding sync

  • Long polls no longer drain the database connection pool.
  • The legacy MSC3575 implementation is removed, which fixes missed list room updates.
  • Superseded requests stop quietly instead of logging foreign key violations.

Fixes

  • Identical state events sent by another user no longer bypass the auth rules.
  • m.room.member state events now go through the membership flows.
  • Unreachable remote profiles answer 502 and the failure is cached.

Release notes: https://codefloe.com/pat-s/zendrite/releases/tag/v3.9.0
Chat: #dendrite:matrix.org

🔗Synapse (website)

Synapse is a Matrix homeserver implementation developed by Element.

madlittlemods (Eric Eastwood) says

This week we have a new release, Synapse 1.165.0. To highlight:

  • We now have an initial, experimental implementation for efficient Server Announcements in Synapse. Server Announcements are for when an admin wants to message everyone on the server all at once (like announcing maintenance windows, policy changes, or incident notices), whereas the existing Service Notices are for admins to message people one by one (not efficient when you want to message everyone). There are still some rough edges that you can track in the epic, but it mostly just works for a client like Element Web.
  • The media download endpoints now skip reading from disk for HEAD requests so we can respond a lot quicker and avoid the unnecessary disk I/O (#20368, thanks to @JimKnoxx).
  • When using TLS listeners from Synapse itself, we now let the OpenSSL defaults shine through, which allows connections to negotiate the use of the post-quantum hybrid X25519MLKEM768 key-exchange group when supported by your OpenSSL version (#20374, thanks to @bardiharborow).
  • Synapse now prefers the notary response that stays valid longest rather than whichever arrived last. This helps when we receive responses from multiple notary servers which could previously cause event verification to fail (#20406, thanks to @AyeshaWaseemAhmad).

Thank you to all our contributors for helping to make Synapse the best it can be. As always, feel free to stop by #synapse:matrix.org to join in on the discussion, and if you encounter a bug, make sure to report it.

🔗Dept of Clients 📱

🔗Tesseract (website)

Marco says

Hello friends, this is the monthly-ish Tesseract update!

Now in version 0.9.8, several nice matrix goodies have been added:

  • Polls (creating, displaying, voting)
  • Display live location shares.
  • Message galleries (drag and drop more than one image/video/audio to the composer and they will be sent as a gallery)
  • Forwarded messages display a clickable link to the original (per MSC4553).
  • Display per-message profiles (per MSC4144).

Additionally, the login screen now has a 'find server' button that will show the user a list of available homeservers to pick from, fetched from https://joinmatrix.org.

On the UI side: configurable fonts, compact room list, pinned spaces sidebar, and timeline max width for wide screens.

Enjoy ;-)

🔗Sable (website)

F0rest reports

Hi TWIM! Sable here, just wanted to drop a quick note in here that we added support for MSC4495: Selective Presence, and we just released a blog post overview on how we are working on implementing Bundled URL Previews and adding new types of media to previews. Thanks!

🔗Robrix (website)

A high-performance, customizable client for power users. Its signature feature is a workspace layout with dockable tabs for chatting in many rooms and threads side by side. Written from scratch in Rust for all platforms.

Kevin Boos announces

Hi everyone, I'm happy to share the first ever TWIM update for Robrix, our Matrix client that has been in development for over 3 years (oof, didn't realize it had been so long). Robrix runs natively on all major platforms and is written from scratch entirely in Rust, and we do mean from scratch ... we also wrote the whole underlying UI toolkit (Makepad) and the platform abstractions framework (Robius) from scratch in Rust. This gives us unique control over every aspect of the app, including how it integrates with the underlying OS and how its UI behaves and adapts.

Robrix's goal is to be highly performant and efficient for power users, even under heavy use. Our signature "cool feature" is a multi-room dockable tabs layout (kinda like an IDE workspace), which lets you see and interact with as many rooms and threads as you want, all side-by-side. Each space gets its own dedicated layout too, so you can easily switch between custom room layouts on a per-space basis, instantaneously. We also have a neat multi-pane UI that lets you decide how extra room content is displayed, like pinned messages, threads, members list, room info, etc, even on mobile.

Robrix is also very intentional about letting you access any feature and any UI view on any device. So you can get the nice stacked mobile-like view on desktop, as well as the dockable workspace view on your phone or tablet. No limits! For example, you can zoom the UI to 112.8% if you want to, even on your iPhone.

I just got back from The Matrix Conference 2026 where I gave a talk about Robrix and some of our cool future directions, like custom generatable mini-apps that run right alongside your rooms or spaces, with a strict capability-like permissions model to ensure safety.

Since the conference, we've published two more beta releases, the latest one is available here. Some nice features we've added recently include:

  • 🛡️ Moderator tools to report, mute, kick, or ban users, plus a powerful tool to find, select, and delete spam messages
  • 🎨 Support for custom emoji and MXC URI media
  • 😀 Quick reactions, double-tap to react, and a super fast emoji picker and search popup
  • 🔍︎ Filter bubbles for the rooms list, like other clients but more flexible:
    • You can inverse/negate a filter (e.g., "non-low priority rooms") by long-pressing or middle/right-clidking it
    • We have more filters like "mod/admin rooms", and they can be combined in more ways
  • 🚪 When leaving a space, we show a nice hierarchical view for choosing which rooms/subspaces to leave
  • 📲 Tons of nice mobile-centric features: ↕️ auto-hide top & bottom bars when scrolling, and smoother/better virtual keyboard behavior
  • 🤏 Lots of effort to make the UI perfect and space-efficient on narrower screens & windows
  • 💬 Instantly discover and jump to old rooms (that have been tombstoned & replaced) with one tap
  • Android: ⚡ consistent 120Hz smooth refresh rate while animating, which 🔋 auto-reduces when idle to preserve battery
    • Plus support for 32-bit devices, Android 8+
  • ⚙️ Tons of new settings to customize lots of Robrix's UI appearance and behavior

Kindly give Robrix a try, and let us know what you think by joining our Matrix room here: #robius-robrix:matrix.org. I'm adding new features (and taking requests!) all the time.

🔗Nexus (website)

Matrix client made with Flutter and a Gomuks backend.

QuadRadical reports

Hello TWIM! This week, Nexus v1.1.0 is out, with many new features, quickly followed by v1.1.1!

You can grab it from the release page. If you use the Flatpak repo, the nightly builds, or the NixOS module, just update.

Here's what changed in 1.1.0:

  • Threads: You can now read and reply in message threads.
  • Polls: Create polls, vote in them, and end them.
  • Bot commands: Bots that advertise their commands using MSC4391 now get suggestions in the composer, along with a form for each command's options. Most of gomuks' built-in commands are supported too.
  • Room directory: Browse and join public rooms, and publish your own rooms to the directory.
  • Room upgrades: You can now upgrade a room to a newer room version, and rooms with a tombstone show a banner linking to the new room.
  • Account switcher: You can now be signed in to more than one account and switch between them.
  • Space improvements: You can now view a space's own timeline, and add or remove rooms from a space.
  • Custom emoji and stickers: Send emoji and stickers from image packs, and manage your packs in settings.
  • Reaction details: Hover over a reaction to see its shortcode, or open the new reactions popover to see who reacted with what.
  • Locations: Shared locations are now shown in the timeline.
  • Notification settings: Manage your push rules from inside Nexus, and set per-room notification levels from the room menu.
  • matrix: links: Nexus now opens matrix: URIs.
  • Event diffs: Changes to power levels, join rules, server ACLs, pinned messages and other room state now show exactly what changed.
  • Power level colours: Display names are now coloured by power level, with a setting to choose between per power level and per user colours.
  • Power level groups: Related permissions are now grouped in room settings, so you can set them all at once, or expand a group to set each one individually.
  • Weighted search: Emoji, user, room and settings search now put the best matches first.
  • Performance and fixes: Lower memory use, and fixes for read receipts.
  • And, as always, a whole lot of bug fixes 🙂

And in 1.1.1:

  • New media players: Nexus has switched from media_kit to new video and audio players. Videos also no longer autoplay on desktop.
  • Attachment previews: Attachments now show a preview in the composer before you send them.
  • Banned members warning: Before you view a room's banned members for the first time, Nexus warns you that they may have offensive names or avatars.
  • No more Play Services: The Android build was accidentally bundling Google Play Services through the location sharing library introduced in 1.1.0, thought it wasn't used at runtime. That's now fixed.
  • Fixes for crashes when loading audio messages on the Flatpak, and failed audio messages are now handled gracefully.

🔗What's next?

I'll keep fixing bugs as you find them, and keep working through the features that are still missing. If you run into anything, please let me know in #nexus:federated.nexus.

🔗Get involved!

If you want to help with development, report bugs, ask questions, or simply keep up with new features, join our Matrix room at #Nexus Client (https://matrix.to/#/!bdbbTYhctZTWzoTzn9:federated.nexus), or check out the Git repo at https://nexus.federated.nexus.

🔗Commet (website)

Commet is a client for mobile and desktop with a modern UI and fun features!

airyz reports

We recently released versions 0.5.1 and 0.5.2 of Commet!

v0.5.1 was mostly focused on some improvements to voice chat, we added an on screen overlay showing activity in your current call (supported on windows, x11 and wayland), and added support for system audio capture when screen sharing on Windows. it also contains a bunch of other small improvements, and is more optimized to use less resources in the background.

🔗Dept of VoIP 🤙

🔗LiveKit JWT service (website)

Bridging Matrix and LiveKit for Matrix RTC realtime sessions.

Johannes Marbach announces

lk-jwt-service 0.10.0 has been released and brings a bunch of important changes.

Most prominently, MSC4195 finally landed. 🎉 As a result, this release adds support for the stable Client-Server endpoints as per the merged version of the MSC. The unstable Client-Server endpoints and the legacy standalone endpoints remain supported in addition.

⚠️ IMPORTANT DEPRECATION NOTICES: Serving the Client-Server endpoints as per the MSC requires setting up lk-jwt-service as an application service on the homeserver. Since the MSC has been accepted, not running as an application service is deprecated as of this release and support for it will be removed in future versions. Details on how to configure the application service can be found in README.md. For the same reason, fronting more than one homeserver via LIVEKIT_FULL_ACCESS_HOMESERVERS is deprecated as well and will be removed in future versions. This setting already only affects the legacy endpoints. For security reasons it is strongly recommended to only put the one homeserver that lk-jwt-service was set up as an application service for into LIVEKIT_FULL_ACCESS_HOMESERVERS.

A last-minute change in the MSC was to RECOMMEND granting publishing permissions to remote users. This acts as a fallback and allows users to join sessions even if their own homeserver doesn't provide an SFU. Server operators can granularly control whether to allow remote publishing with the new LIVEKIT_REMOTE_CAN_PUBLISH_HOMESERVERS environment variable.

A related change in the final MSC was to RECOMMEND disabling the permission to update one's own metadata for participants. The service now disables this permission by default on tokens. Admins that rely on this feature, may reenable the permission with the new LIVEKIT_CAN_UPDATE_OWN_METADATA environment variable.

MSC4196 also landed and to support the transition to its stable identifiers, the service now maps m.call#ROOM slot IDs to m.call#room. This means clients will end up in the same LiveKit room regardless of which spelling they used.

Finally, lk-jwt-service is now able to bind to a Unix socket via the LIVEKIT_JWT_BIND environment variable. Thanks to GitHub user @cyberb for contributing this feature.

🔗Dept of Ops 🛠

🔗Connectivity Tester

MTRNord (they/them) announces

A homeserver report now covers more than basic federation reachability, so there are more choices about what to run and more detail to make sense of afterwards. Here are a few highlights from the latest release.

🔗Pick the Checks You Need

The homepage has a "What to check" picker. Outgoing federation, Client API / Matrix 2.0, MatrixRTC / Element Call, and Neoboard can be selected separately. The result then shows tabs for the categories you chose, instead of making you scroll through checks you did not run. Alerts and probe jobs also have federation-only, standard, and extended presets.

Some checks are useful when you need a closer look:

  • The room-version check reports which Matrix room versions a homeserver accepts. It sends a signed synthetic federation invite for each version, so the picker labels it as making extra requests.
  • The experimental MSC4496 calendar check looks for the client and federation availability endpoints. It only checks whether those routes exist; it does not request calendar data.
  • The MatrixRTC results show whether the server advertises sticky events (MSC4354), which Neoboard's LiveKit mode and Element Call's Matrix 2.0 mode need.

🔗Read Connectivity Results More Easily

The results page opens with a health summary. When you scroll down, a slim bar keeps the server name and the main results in view. Section headers show useful status without opening them, and the connectivity section starts with the number of working addresses, TLS versions, and whether ECH is enabled.

Certificates are grouped instead of repeated for every IP, while each address has its own collapsible details. When a server advertises Encrypted Client Hello, the tester also verifies the public-name certificate a client sees if its ECH attempt is rejected. The report for mtrnord.blog shows that certificate alongside the regular one.

🔗Alerts for Unsteady Connections and ECH

Alerts now confirm an outage from a window of recent checks: three failures in the last five checks by default. A single successful check during an unreliable spell therefore does not reset the whole confirmation. If a server keeps flipping between down and recovered, its status and history still update, but down/recovered emails and webhooks are suppressed while it is flapping. The recent checks and transitions are saved with the alert, so a restart does not reset that decision. The alerts overview also shows down and recovered changes live.

Outgoing federation checks also need strong evidence before they treat an address family as unsupported. Even when that result is cached, a background probe keeps checking for recovery. Alerts that have stayed down for more than a week are checked hourly, so recovery is still noticed without running a full check every minute.

ECH is covered by alert notifications too. For alerts with TLS expiry warnings enabled, the sooner expiring of the regular and ECH public-name certificates sets the warning date. If the ECH certificate expires first, the email and webhook name its public name. A replaced ECH certificate can also trigger the TLS certificate-change notification when that option is enabled.

🔗Share a Report

The actions are together in one place: get a permalink, re-run the check, or open the Export menu. Markdown now follows the report's sections, including the overview, problems, and individual checks. The redesigned PDF has a light theme for printing and a dark theme for screens, with a verdict banner and compact stat cards.

Try it at https://connectivity-tester.mtrnord.blog/. The changelog, source code, and support forum have more details and a place for feedback.
